title: AA Batteries 8-pack

drivers.name: Price increase (5.5% above regular)
drivers.evidence: Same price last week (2026-10-05) sold 31 units (x0.89 vs baseline); historical price sensitivity implies ~10-12% demand drop at 5.5% price hike.

drivers.name: TikTok trend (new driver)
drivers.evidence: No past occurrences of TikTok trend; noise-adjusted estimate shrunk toward 1.0; plausible uplift if viral, but uncertain. Used moderate uplift based on potential reach.

adjustment.analysis: The baseline median is 34.9. No events or promotions are scheduled. The price is 5.5% above regular, which typically suppresses demand. Past 30% off promotions lifted sales by a median 31% vs baseline, but this is a 5.5% price increase, not a discount. The TikTok trend is a new driver with no historical precedent; the noise-adjusted effect of such trends is typically low unless proven. The classical uplift model suggests no effect, consistent with the lack of known drivers. The recent week with same price (2026-10-05) sold 31 units (x0.89 vs baseline), suggesting a price penalty. No evidence of pantry loading or seasonal ramp. The forecast should reflect a slight downside from price and uncertain trend.

STATISTICAL BASELINE (exponential smoothing of recent sales; it ignores events, promotions and prices):
  median 34.9 | 5%-95%: 18.5 - 58.2 | 10%-90%: 20.9 - 55.2

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-44% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
